Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the InnovateCloud Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. [Operator Instructions] Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Jessica Morales, Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Jessica Morales:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to InnovateCloud's Q3 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Thompson, CEO; David Lee, CFO; Michael Chen, CTO; Emily Carter, Chief Revenue Officer; Jason Ramirez, Chief Product Officer; Olivia Wilson, Chief Marketing Officer; and Brian Nguyen, Chief Customer Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Thompson.

Alex Thompson:
Thank you, Jessica, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on InnovateCloud's performance for Q3. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our ClarityAI and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on eight key areas: Cost of revenue breakdown, Full-year revenue guidance, Average contract value (ACV), Churn analysis, NRR performance, Product roadmap, Rule of 40, and Free cash flow.

Alright, good morning everyone. I'm Sarah Chen, VP of Finance here at InnovateCloud. As we move to the cost of revenue discussion, I want to provide a detailed breakdown and context for our figures this quarter. Understanding the composition of our cost of revenue is crucial for gauging the scalability and efficiency of our business model, particularly in the dynamic SaaS landscape.

Our total cost of revenue for Q3 came in at $45 million, a 20% increase year-over-year. While this increase aligns with our overall revenue growth of 25%, it's crucial to understand the underlying drivers. Let's break down the key components:

1. Hosting Infrastructure & Cloud Services (45% of Cost of Revenue):

This constitutes the largest portion of our cost of revenue, totaling $20.25 million. This is primarily driven by our reliance on AWS for hosting our core InnovateCloud platform and the associated databases. This includes:

*   Compute Costs (EC2, Lambda, etc.): This is where we see the biggest fluctuation quarter-to-quarter. We experienced a 22% YoY increase in compute costs, largely due to the expansion of our enterprise customer base and their heavier usage of our AI-powered analytics features. These customers, like our recent win with GlobalCorp, require dedicated instances and higher processing power.
*   Storage Costs (S3, EBS, etc.): Storage costs remain relatively stable, increasing by 15% YoY, reflecting the continued organic growth in data being stored within our platform.
*   Networking Costs (Data Transfer, VPN, etc.): Networking costs are up 18% YoY. This increase is partially attributable to the expansion of our presence in the APAC region, requiring more robust and geographically diverse data transfer capabilities. We are also seeing increased bandwidth usage as we roll out our new video collaboration features integrated into InnovateCloud Pro.

Technical Initiatives: We are actively pursuing several technical initiatives to optimize our hosting costs.

    *   Auto-Scaling Optimization: We are implementing more sophisticated auto-scaling policies across our AWS infrastructure to dynamically adjust resource allocation based on real-time demand. We expect this to yield a 5-7% reduction in compute costs over the next two quarters. We are utilizing tools like CloudWatch and Datadog to monitor resource utilization and fine-tune our scaling parameters.
    *   Serverless Architecture Adoption: We are strategically migrating some of our less critical workloads to serverless architectures (AWS Lambda) to reduce idle resource consumption. We've seen promising results with our initial pilot project, achieving a 10% cost reduction in that specific area.
    *   Reserved Instance Optimization: We are continuously reviewing and optimizing our reserved instance (RI) portfolio to ensure we are leveraging the maximum discounts available from AWS. We are employing tools that automatically identify and recommend RI purchases based on our usage patterns.

2. Customer Support (30% of Cost of Revenue):

Customer support expenses accounted for $13.5 million. This includes salaries, benefits, and technology costs associated with our global support teams.

*   Tier 1 Support: This is our frontline support, handling basic inquiries and troubleshooting. We've seen a slight increase in Tier 1 support requests, primarily related to onboarding new users onto our InnovateCloud Essentials package.
*   Tier 2/3 Support: These teams handle more complex technical issues and escalations. We've observed a decrease in Tier 2/3 support requests, which we attribute to the improved stability and user-friendliness of our latest platform release. This is a positive sign, indicating that our engineering efforts are paying off.
*   Support Technology: We've invested in AI-powered chatbots and knowledge base solutions to improve the efficiency of our support operations. These investments are beginning to yield results, allowing us to handle a higher volume of inquiries with the same number of support agents.
*   Regional Commentary: Our support costs are higher in North America and Europe due to higher labor costs. We are exploring options for expanding our support presence in regions with lower labor costs, such as India and the Philippines, while maintaining our high standards of service quality.

Strategic Insights: We are closely monitoring our Net Promoter Score (NPS) and customer satisfaction (CSAT) scores to ensure that our support investments are delivering a positive return. We are also analyzing support ticket data to identify areas where we can improve our product and documentation to reduce the need for support in the first place. We are investing in proactive customer success programs, similar to what companies like Salesforce and HubSpot do, to anticipate and address customer needs before they become problems.

3. Professional Services & Onboarding (15% of Cost of Revenue):

This category, totaling $6.75 million, covers the costs associated with deploying and customizing our software for enterprise clients. This includes:

*   Implementation Consultants: Salaries and travel expenses for our consultants who work on-site with clients to configure InnovateCloud to their specific needs.
*   Training Materials: Costs associated with creating and delivering training programs for our clients' users.
*   Custom Development: Expenses related to developing custom integrations and features for specific clients.

Technical Initiatives: We are actively working to reduce the cost of professional services by developing more standardized implementation methodologies and self-service onboarding tools. We are leveraging technologies like low-code/no-code platforms (like OutSystems) to enable our clients to customize InnovateCloud themselves, reducing the need for custom development.

4. Third-Party Software & Licensing (10% of Cost of Revenue):

This represents the smallest portion of our cost of revenue, at $4.5 million. This includes licenses for third-party tools that are integrated into our platform, such as analytics libraries, security software, and CRM integrations.

Strategic Insights: We are continuously evaluating our third-party software portfolio to ensure we are getting the best value for our money. We are also exploring opportunities to develop our own alternatives to some of these tools, which could potentially reduce our reliance on third-party vendors in the long run.

Overall Trends and Outlook:

While our cost of revenue is increasing in line with our revenue growth, we are committed to improving our efficiency and scalability. The technical initiatives I outlined above are expected to generate significant cost savings over the next several quarters. We are also closely monitoring our customer acquisition cost (CAC) and customer lifetime value (LTV) to ensure that our investments in sales and marketing are generating a positive return.

We believe that by focusing on these key areas, we can continue to deliver strong revenue growth while maintaining healthy gross margins and driving long-term shareholder value. We are confident that InnovateCloud is well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for cloud-based software solutions.

That concludes my breakdown of our cost of revenue. I'm happy to answer any questions you may have.

Okay, good morning everyone, and thank you for joining us for our Q4 and Full Year 2023 Earnings Call. As always, I'm Sarah Chen, CFO of InnovateCloud, and I'll be providing the financial overview today, focusing particularly on our full-year 2024 revenue guidance.

Full-Year 2024 Revenue Guidance: A Deep Dive

After a strong close to 2023, marked by accelerated adoption of our AI-powered analytics suite, "ClarityAI," and continued expansion in the EMEA region, we are initiating our full-year 2024 revenue guidance with a projected range of $875 million to $900 million. This represents a projected year-over-year growth rate of 22% to 25% compared to our actual 2023 revenue of $715 million.

Let's break down the key drivers and underlying assumptions behind this guidance:

1. Organic Growth in Core SaaS Offerings (60% of Projected Revenue):

    *   ClarityAI (Analytics Suite): We anticipate ClarityAI to be a significant growth engine, contributing approximately 35% of the overall revenue growth. This expectation is based on several factors:

        *   Expanded Feature Set: We're launching "ClarityAI Pro" in Q2 2024, offering advanced predictive modeling and personalized recommendations tailor-made for the financial services sector. This premium tier, priced at a 30% higher ARR (Annual Recurring Revenue), is expected to drive up average deal size. We are seeing strong initial interest in this release from financial institutions that are looking to compete with the likes of Palantir.
        *   Increased Customer Stickiness: Early data from our initial ClarityAI adopters demonstrates a churn rate nearly 40% lower than our overall average, indicating strong product-market fit and compelling value proposition. This is due to the AI-powered features automating tasks that used to require a dedicated data science team.
        *   Strategic Partnerships: We're expanding our integrations with leading CRM and ERP platforms, like Salesforce and NetSuite, making ClarityAI a more seamless and powerful tool for our customers. These integrations are crucial for streamlining workflows and making our solution a "must-have" rather than a "nice-to-have."
    *   Legacy SaaS Products (Core Platform): While ClarityAI is driving significant growth, our core SaaS platform, which includes project management and collaboration tools, is expected to contribute steady growth of around 10%. This growth will be fueled by:

        *   Seat Expansion: We're focused on expanding our user base within existing accounts, leveraging our customer success team to identify and address unmet needs.
        *   Strategic Pricing Adjustments: We implemented a modest price increase of 5% in Q4 2023, which we expect to contribute to revenue growth in 2024.
        *   Bundling of Core Products: We are exploring bundling options together to allow for a better price point for customers.

2. Expansion in EMEA and APAC Regions (25% of Projected Revenue):

    *   EMEA: Our EMEA operations saw a 40% increase in revenue in 2023, and we expect this momentum to continue in 2024, albeit at a slightly more moderate pace of around 30%. This growth will be driven by:

        *   Localized Marketing Campaigns: We're investing in localized marketing campaigns that resonate with specific cultural nuances and regulatory requirements in key European markets, such as Germany and France.
        *   Strategic Partnerships: We're building strategic partnerships with local system integrators and consulting firms to expand our reach and provide on-the-ground support to our customers.
        *   Data Residency Compliance: We have successfully achieved GDPR compliance and are actively working on certifications for other regional data privacy regulations to alleviate customer concerns and unlock new market opportunities. We expect to achieve FedRAMP compliance by Q3 2024. This will allow for new opportunities for us to sell to the US Government.
    *   APAC: While still a relatively small portion of our overall revenue, our APAC region is showing promising growth (around 35% projected). We are focusing on key markets like Australia and Singapore, where we see strong demand for cloud-based solutions. The main focus here will be to build out infrastructure for the region.

3. Strategic Acquisitions and Partnerships (15% of Projected Revenue):

    *   Potential Acquisitions: We are actively evaluating potential acquisition targets that align with our strategic priorities, particularly in the areas of AI and machine learning. While we have not factored any specific acquisitions into our initial guidance, we believe that a successful acquisition could provide a significant boost to our revenue growth in 2024.
    *   Strategic Partnerships: We are seeking to expand our partner network to include more integration partnerships, and reseller partnerships to increase our scale.

4. Key Assumptions and Considerations:

    *   Economic Outlook: Our guidance assumes a moderate economic slowdown in the second half of 2024. We are closely monitoring macroeconomic indicators and are prepared to adjust our guidance if necessary.
    *   Competition: The SaaS market is highly competitive, and we face increasing competition from both established players like Microsoft and Atlassian, as well as emerging startups. We are investing heavily in product innovation and customer success to maintain our competitive edge.
    *   Sales Execution: Our ability to achieve our revenue targets depends on our sales team's ability to effectively execute our sales strategy and close deals. We are investing in sales training and enablement to improve our sales performance.
    *   Customer Churn: We have factored in a modest increase in customer churn due to the economic slowdown, but we are confident that our strong customer relationships and compelling value proposition will help us to mitigate this risk.
    *   FX fluctuations: Given our international expansion, we are closely monitoring FX fluctuations. We have incorporated a conservative estimate of potential negative impacts from currency headwinds into our guidance.

Technical Initiatives Supporting Growth:

    *   Microservices Architecture: We are continuing our transition to a microservices architecture, which will improve the scalability, reliability, and agility of our platform. This will enable us to deliver new features and updates more quickly and efficiently.
    *   AI/ML Infrastructure: We are investing in our AI/ML infrastructure to support the continued development and deployment of AI-powered features across our product portfolio. This includes building a dedicated data science team and investing in cutting-edge hardware and software.
    *   Security Enhancements: We are committed to maintaining the highest standards of security and compliance. We are investing in security enhancements across our platform to protect our customers' data and maintain their trust.

Conclusion:

We are confident that our strong product portfolio, strategic investments, and talented team will enable us to achieve our full-year 2024 revenue guidance. We are committed to delivering sustainable, profitable growth and creating value for our shareholders. We will be closely monitoring market conditions and are prepared to adjust our guidance as needed.

Now, I'd be happy to answer any questions you may have.

Okay, let's dive into a detailed discussion about our Average Contract Value (ACV) performance, a key metric we closely monitor at [Fictional SaaS Company Name], or [FSC] for short.

Good morning, everyone. As we move into the discussion of our Q2 2024 earnings, I want to address a critical metric: Average Contract Value, or ACV. As you know, ACV represents the average annualized revenue generated from each customer contract. It's a vital indicator of our ability to upsell, cross-sell, and attract larger enterprise clients, directly impacting our ARR growth and overall profitability.

Q2 2024 ACV Performance:

*   Reported ACV: In Q2 2024, our ACV stood at $45,000, representing a 6% increase year-over-year compared to $42,500 in Q2 2023. This is a positive trend and reflects the successful execution of our strategic initiatives.
*   Sequential Growth: We also saw a 2% increase sequentially from Q1 2024's ACV of $44,100. While moderate, this indicates continued momentum and a healthy pipeline.

Key Trends Driving ACV Growth:

1. Enterprise Focus & Product Bundling: One of the primary drivers of the ACV increase is our strategic focus on acquiring and expanding within larger enterprise accounts. We've seen significant traction with our "Enterprise Security Suite" offering, a bundled solution that combines our core threat detection platform with advanced vulnerability management and incident response capabilities. This bundle, introduced late last year, carries a higher price point and has been particularly attractive to companies in the financial services and healthcare sectors, who are facing increasing regulatory pressures similar to those seen by Atlassian and Crowdstrike. We saw a 35% attach rate of the Enterprise Security Suite to new enterprise deals in Q2, significantly boosting ACV.

2. Premium Feature Adoption: We've observed a growing adoption of our premium features, particularly within our AI-powered analytics module. This module, which uses machine learning to provide predictive threat intelligence and automate security workflows, commands a premium price. We see a direct correlation between customers who adopt the AI module and a 15-20% increase in their overall ACV within the first year.

3. Multi-Product Expansion: Our customers are increasingly adopting multiple [FSC] products. Our platform strategy, designed around seamless integration and data sharing across different security domains, is resonating well. The average customer now uses 2.3 [FSC] products, compared to 1.9 a year ago. This cross-selling activity is a key contributor to ACV growth. We're taking a cue from companies like Salesforce and ServiceNow who have successfully expanded platform offerings over time.

4. Price Optimization: We implemented a targeted price optimization strategy in Q1, focusing on specific product tiers and add-on features. This involved analyzing usage patterns, competitive pricing, and perceived value to adjust our pricing structure accordingly. We believe this has contributed to the Q2 ACV growth, without negatively impacting renewal rates, which remain above 90%.

Regional Commentary:

*   North America: Remains our strongest region, accounting for over 60% of our revenue. ACV growth in North America was 8% year-over-year, driven by strong demand from the financial services and technology sectors.
*   EMEA: We are seeing increasing traction in the EMEA region, particularly in the UK and Germany. While ACV growth in EMEA was slightly lower than North America at 5%, we are encouraged by the expanding pipeline and increasing brand awareness. We have invested in localized sales and marketing efforts to better address the specific needs of European customers, including GDPR compliance features.
*   APAC: APAC is our fastest-growing region, although it still represents a smaller portion of our overall revenue. ACV growth in APAC was 12% year-over-year, driven by strong demand from the manufacturing and e-commerce sectors. We are expanding our partner network in APAC to accelerate growth in this region.

Technical Initiatives Impacting ACV:

*   Enhanced API Integrations: We've invested heavily in improving our API integrations with leading SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) and SOAR (Security Orchestration, Automation and Response) platforms like Splunk and Palo Alto Networks' Cortex XSOAR. These integrations make our platform more valuable to enterprise customers who already have existing security investments, driving higher ACV.
*   Improved Onboarding Experience: We've simplified our onboarding process with personalized implementation plans and dedicated success managers for larger accounts. This reduces time-to-value and increases customer satisfaction, leading to higher renewal rates and opportunities for upsells.
*   Platform Scalability & Performance: Continued investments in our infrastructure have ensured that our platform can handle the increasing demands of our growing customer base. This is particularly important for enterprise customers who rely on our platform for mission-critical security operations. Think of this in the same way that Amazon Web Services thinks of availability and scalability.

Strategic Insights and Future Outlook:

*   Continued Focus on Enterprise: We will continue to prioritize the acquisition of larger enterprise accounts. We are investing in our enterprise sales team and developing targeted marketing campaigns to reach these customers.
*   Expand Product Portfolio: We are actively exploring opportunities to expand our product portfolio through strategic acquisitions and internal development. We are particularly interested in areas such as cloud security and data loss prevention.
*   Strengthen Partner Ecosystem: We will continue to build and strengthen our partner ecosystem. We believe that partners are essential for expanding our reach and delivering value to our customers.
*   Data-Driven Upselling: We're implementing a more sophisticated data-driven approach to identifying upselling opportunities. By analyzing customer usage patterns and identifying unmet needs, we can proactively offer solutions that drive value and increase ACV.

Looking ahead, we anticipate continued ACV growth in the second half of 2024. We expect to see further traction with our Enterprise Security Suite, increased adoption of our premium features, and continued success in cross-selling our products. While macroeconomic conditions remain uncertain, we believe that our strong value proposition and strategic focus on enterprise accounts will enable us to continue to deliver strong results.

In conclusion, the trends in our ACV are encouraging and reflect the strength of our platform, our strategic focus on enterprise accounts, and our commitment to delivering value to our customers. We are confident that we can continue to drive ACV growth in the future.

I'm now happy to take any questions you may have regarding our ACV performance.

Okay, let's dive into our churn analysis for Q3 2023. This is a critical area of focus for us, and we want to be transparent about our performance and the actions we're taking.

Overall Churn Performance:

Our Q3 gross dollar retention (GDR) came in at 91.5%, which translates to a churn rate of 8.5%. While still within our acceptable range, it's slightly above our target of 90% GDR (10% churn) and marks a 0.7 percentage point increase from Q2's 92.2% GDR. This warrants a deeper look. Net dollar retention (NDR) for Q3 was 115%, indicating strong expansion within our existing customer base, which partially offsets the churn impact. However, reducing churn remains a top priority to maximize the overall lifetime value of our customer base.

Segmented Churn Analysis:

We break down churn across several key dimensions: customer size (ARR bands), product line, industry vertical, and geographic region. This granular approach allows us to pinpoint specific areas needing attention.

*   ARR Band: We observed the highest churn rate (12.3%) in our smallest ARR band (customers paying under $10,000 annually). This is often attributed to smaller businesses with tighter budgets being more susceptible to economic downturns, as well as potentially lacking the internal resources to fully utilize our platform. We're seeing some direct competition from lower-priced, less feature-rich solutions in this segment, similar to companies like Freshworks offering alternatives to some of our core functionalities. Conversely, our largest customers (>$100,000 ARR) exhibited the lowest churn at 3.8%, demonstrating the stickiness of our platform within enterprise environments.

*   Product Line: Churn varied significantly across our product offerings. Our flagship CRM platform, "Synergy," maintained a low churn rate of 6.2%. However, our newer marketing automation module, "Momentum," experienced a higher churn of 10.5%. This is concerning, and we believe it stems from a combination of factors: a steeper learning curve for users, integration challenges with some legacy marketing systems, and a competitive landscape dominated by established players like HubSpot and Marketo. We also saw a slight uptick in churn in our older "Legacy" product line as customers migrated to newer solutions, or off the platform entirely.

*   Industry Vertical: The retail sector showed the highest churn (11.8%) in Q3. We believe this is directly correlated to the ongoing challenges retailers face with shifting consumer behavior and increased competition from e-commerce giants like Amazon. The financial services sector, on the other hand, remained a stronghold with a low churn rate of 4.5%, indicating the critical role our platform plays in their regulatory compliance and customer data management.

*   Geographic Region: North America continues to be our strongest region with the lowest churn (7.1%). However, we observed a concerning increase in churn in the EMEA region, particularly in the UK and Germany, reaching 9.8%. This may be attributed to increased competition from European-based SaaS providers, as well as specific GDPR-related compliance concerns that some smaller companies are struggling with, leading them to opt for simpler, more localized solutions.

Reasons for Churn:

We conduct exit interviews and analyze customer feedback data to understand the underlying reasons for churn. The top three reasons consistently cited in Q3 were:

1. Lack of Perceived Value (35%): Customers stated that they weren't realizing the ROI they expected from our platform. This often boiled down to insufficient training, poor onboarding experiences, or a mismatch between their needs and the platform's capabilities. We're seeing this particularly with customers who purchased Momentum.
2. Technical Issues/Integration Challenges (28%): Integration with existing systems, particularly for customers using older versions of SAP or Oracle, continues to be a pain point. We also saw some customers citing performance issues and bugs, particularly during peak usage times.
3. Price Sensitivity/Competition (22%): While our pricing is competitive, some customers, especially in the smaller ARR band and in price-sensitive markets like Latin America, are opting for cheaper alternatives, even if they offer fewer features.

Mitigation Strategies:

We're implementing a multi-pronged approach to address these churn drivers:

*   Enhanced Onboarding and Training: We're investing heavily in improving our onboarding process. This includes:

    *   Personalized Onboarding Plans: Tailoring onboarding based on customer size, industry, and specific use cases. We're leveraging data analytics to identify customers at high risk of churn early on and proactively offering additional support.
    *   Interactive Training Modules: We're transitioning from static documentation to interactive training modules and video tutorials. We're also launching a new "Synergy Certified Professional" program to equip users with the skills they need to maximize the value of our platform.
    *   Dedicated Customer Success Managers (CSMs): We're increasing the ratio of CSMs to customers, particularly for those in the higher ARR bands and using complex modules like Momentum.

*   Technical Improvements and Integration Focus: We're prioritizing the following technical initiatives:

    *   Performance Optimization: We're investing in infrastructure upgrades and code optimization to improve platform performance and stability, particularly during peak usage. Our engineering team is working on containerizing key services using Kubernetes to improve scalability and resilience.
    *   API Enhancements: We're expanding our API capabilities to simplify integration with a wider range of third-party systems, including popular marketing automation platforms and ERP solutions. We are launching standardized connectors for the most requested ERP and legacy systems.
    *   Bug Fixes and Feature Requests: We're accelerating our bug fix cycle and prioritizing feature requests based on customer feedback. We have a dedicated team focused on addressing Momentum integration pain points.

*   Pricing and Packaging Adjustments:

    *   Value-Based Pricing: We're exploring value-based pricing models that align pricing with the actual value customers derive from our platform.
    *   Targeted Discounts: We're offering targeted discounts and promotions to customers in price-sensitive markets.
    *   Tiered Service Packages: We are introducing a more comprehensive range of service packages that include proactive support, training, and consulting services, allowing customers to choose the level of support that best meets their needs.

*   Regional Strategies:

    *   EMEA Focus: We're investing in localized marketing campaigns and partnerships in the EMEA region to increase brand awareness and build stronger relationships with local customers. We are also increasing the number of multilingual support staff.
    *   Latin America: We are exploring partnerships with local system integrators to provide implementation and support services in Latin America, to overcome language barriers and cultural differences.

Expected Impact:

We expect these mitigation strategies to begin showing results in Q4 2023 and continue to improve our churn performance into 2024. We are closely monitoring key metrics such as customer satisfaction scores, product usage, and support ticket volume to track the effectiveness of our initiatives. We are committed to reducing churn and maximizing the lifetime value of our customer base. We believe that by addressing the root causes of churn and investing in customer success, we can achieve our long-term growth objectives.

We are open to questions regarding our churn analysis and mitigation strategies. Thank you.

Okay, good morning everyone. Let's dive into our Net Revenue Retention (NRR) performance for Q2 2024. NRR remains a critical indicator of our success, reflecting our ability to retain and expand our existing customer base.

Q2 2024 NRR Performance: 118%

We are pleased to report an NRR of 118% for the second quarter. This represents a slight decrease of 2 percentage points from Q1\u2019s 120%, but remains well above our target of 110% and industry benchmarks, particularly in a climate where macro-economic headwinds are impacting expansion budgets across the sector. Companies like Salesforce and Workday, while still posting healthy NRR, have also noted a slight moderation in expansion rates recently. We attribute our strong performance to a continued focus on customer success, strategic product development, and targeted account management.

Breaking Down the Drivers:

Let's break down the key components driving our NRR:

*   Expansion Revenue (Upselling & Cross-selling): 25% Contribution to NRR

    *   Expansion revenue contributed 25 percentage points to our NRR. This demonstrates our success in upselling existing customers to higher-tier plans and cross-selling additional modules within our platform, "InnoSuite". The growth in expansion is driven primarily by:

        *   Adoption of the "InnoSuite Analytics" Module: We saw a particularly strong uptake of our \u201cInnoSuite Analytics\u201d module (released in late Q4 2023) which leverages AI-powered insights to optimize our customers' workflows. We've seen a 35% adoption rate among existing "InnoSuite Core" customers in the last two quarters. This module commands a premium price point, contributing significantly to expansion. We are seeing this module perform particularly well amongst our EMEA based clients, who are seeking to comply with stringent GDPR regulations.
        *   Upselling to "Enterprise" Tier: We successfully migrated a significant number of mid-market clients to our "Enterprise" tier, which offers enhanced features, dedicated support, and higher usage limits. A key driver here was the introduction of our "Data Residency" feature, allowing Enterprise customers to choose the geographical location of their data storage, addressing concerns of larger, multinational organizations.
        *   Strategic Partnerships: Our strategic partnerships with consulting firms like Accenture and Deloitte have proven effective in identifying upselling opportunities within our existing customer base. They are able to identify opportunities for customers to improve their workflow.
        *   Technical Initiatives: We implemented a new \u201cusage-based recommendation engine\u201d within the InnoSuite platform. This engine analyzes user behavior and proactively suggests relevant modules or feature upgrades, leading to a 15% uplift in expansion conversations initiated by our sales team.
*   Contraction Revenue: (5%) Impact on NRR

    *   Contraction negatively impacted our NRR by 5 percentage points. This reflects instances where customers downgraded their plans, reduced user licenses, or scaled back their usage of certain modules. Several key themes are driving this:

        *   Macroeconomic Headwinds: As mentioned earlier, the current macroeconomic environment is impacting some of our customers, particularly in the retail and manufacturing sectors. Several clients have implemented cost-cutting measures, leading to reduced software budgets. We are actively working with these customers to identify ways to optimize their usage and demonstrate the value of InnoSuite even in a challenging economic climate.
        *   Platform Optimization We are focusing on building out the platform to better serve the needs of smaller businesses, who might have previously been sold plans that were too large for their needs.
        *   Competitive Pressure: We are seeing increased competition from point solutions, particularly in specific areas like project management and CRM. While InnoSuite offers a comprehensive platform, some customers are opting for specialized tools that address niche needs. We are responding by strengthening our integrations with these point solutions and highlighting the benefits of a unified platform.
*   Churn Revenue: (2%) Impact on NRR

    *   Churn contributed 2 percentage points to the negative impact on NRR. This represents the percentage of recurring revenue lost due to customer cancellations. We are consistently maintaining a low churn rate. Key factors contributing to this low churn:

        *   Robust Customer Success Program: Our proactive customer success program, which includes onboarding support, training resources, and regular check-in calls, is instrumental in ensuring customer satisfaction and preventing churn. We have recently invested in a new "Customer Health Score" system that allows us to identify at-risk customers early and proactively address their concerns.
        *   High Switching Costs: Switching from InnoSuite to a competitor involves significant data migration and workflow disruption. This creates a natural barrier to churn. We continue to invest in making our platform "sticky" by offering valuable features and integrations that are difficult to replicate.
        *    Focus on Customer Satisfaction: Our regular NPS surveys and feedback loops help us identify areas for improvement and ensure that we are meeting the evolving needs of our customers. We have recently implemented changes to our support processes based on customer feedback, resulting in a significant improvement in customer satisfaction scores.

Regional Commentary:

We are seeing variations in NRR performance across different regions:

*   North America: NRR in North America remains strong at 120%, driven by high adoption rates of InnoSuite Analytics and strong expansion within the financial services sector.
*   EMEA: While the "InnoSuite Analytics" module has performed very well, NRR in EMEA is slightly below the company average at 115%, primarily due to macroeconomic headwinds impacting customers in the UK and Germany.
*   APAC: NRR in APAC is showing steady growth at 112%, with strong adoption in the technology and e-commerce sectors. We are investing in expanding our sales and marketing presence in this region to capitalize on the growing demand for cloud-based software solutions.

Strategic Insights & Outlook:

Looking ahead, we remain focused on sustaining our strong NRR performance by:

*   Continuing to invest in product innovation: We are developing new modules and features that address the evolving needs of our customers, with a particular focus on AI-powered capabilities and industry-specific solutions.
*   Strengthening our customer success program: We are expanding our customer success team and investing in new tools and processes to ensure that all of our customers are realizing the full value of InnoSuite.
*   Expanding our partnerships: We are actively seeking new partnerships with consulting firms and technology providers to expand our reach and provide our customers with a more comprehensive solution.
*   Proactive Customer Engagement: We are closely monitoring the macroeconomic environment and proactively engaging with customers who may be at risk of contraction or churn.

While we acknowledge the potential impact of macroeconomic headwinds, we are confident that our strong product, customer success program, and strategic partnerships will enable us to maintain a healthy NRR and drive long-term growth. We believe our continued investment in these areas will position us favorably against competitors like Atlassian and Monday.com, even as they face similar pressures.

We will continue to monitor our NRR performance closely and provide updates on our progress in future earnings calls. Thank you.
